C-APPROVE-TIME-REVIEW.Summary: Four concerns, named together because the scope is deliberate rather than accreted: (1) teach ngrace review --change as a step before ngrace gate approve at spec-approve and at plan-approve (F149); (2) teach what a clean approve-time review looks like, including the partial-review caveat and the expected scope findings, and never widen ObservedWriteScope to silence them (F150); (3) show the closed approval lexicon whenever ratification of a written spec or plan is requested, one request per message naming one artifact, and record the phrase verbatim (F152); (4) give the XML-escaping rule a hard-rule home in ngrace-spec and ngrace-plan (F43). This bundle does not change review detectors and does not widen the closed lexicon.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-BEFORE-APPROVE: After a sufficient lexicon phrase and before ngrace gate approve, ngrace-spec <status_rules> and workflow step 6, and ngrace-plan <must_do> rule 15, instruct ngrace review --path . --change C-ID (does not record a verdict). Rule 15 is amended in place; requirement numbers 16 and 17 do not shift. ngrace-reviewer <mechanized_first> names three moments: spec-approve, plan-approve, and before close judgment, and keeps the same worked invocation. Existing pins remain: spec "that command writes status"; plan "the gate writes status and records the fingerprint"; reviewer "unfingerprinted Decision silent". Failure conditions: review taught only in reviewer; rule 15 replaced by a new row; execute rule 9 rewritten; gate approve still the first command after the phrase.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXPECTED-FINDINGS: The approve-time review instruction in ngrace-spec, ngrace-plan, and ngrace-reviewer states all of: at spec-approve the scope and WriteEvidence audits report not-run (no plan), and attempt-pair reports ran over 0 pairs — a green covers pattern detectors and artifact checks only, not a scope pass, and a 0-pair attempt-pair is not substantiation; at plan-approve review.scope-outside-write-scope on the bundle's own spec.xml, plan.xml, and (when that file changed on the branch) decisions.md is expected; do not add those paths to ObservedWriteScope to silence the finding. Other findings are not expected-clean. Failure conditions: instruction claims attempt-pair is not-run at spec-approve; instruction omits the scope/WriteEvidence not-run caveat; instruction tells the reader to widen ObservedWriteScope; F149.1's archive firing is taught as expected-clean.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-LEXICON-PROTOCOL: Each of the four LEXICON_SKILLS paths' <approval_lexicon> keeps the closed sufficient set and the named non-approvals, and adds the three F152 rules in that block: show the closed lexicon whenever ratification of a written spec or plan is requested, quoting the sufficient phrases bound to the artifact id and stage in the same breath; one approval request per message, one artifact, nothing else asked; record the ratifying phrase verbatim (the bytes the human wrote, never a paraphrase). Spec versus plan still differ only in "approve this spec" versus "approve this plan" among the sufficient phrases. ngrace-spec workflow step 6 quotes the lexicon bound to C-ID and spec stage. ngrace-plan's approval request does the same for the plan stage. Failure conditions: a copy is updated and another is not; the closed set gains a phrase; F152 rules live only outside the iterated block; step 2 treats a lexicon phrase as gate approve.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-XML-ESCAPE: ngrace-spec and ngrace-plan <hard_rules> (canonical and packaged) state: when a spec, plan, design-context, or skill XML block must name a tag, attribute form, or angle-bracketed token, write it as character data with entities (< > &); do not paraphrase the brackets away to keep the document well-formed; markup-byte assertions belong in a TypeScript test. Failure conditions: only one of the two skills; only canonical; the rule is restated as "do not mention tags".
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CONTRACT-PINS: scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts asserts the new teaching on canonical ngrace-spec, ngrace-plan, and ngrace-reviewer (review before gate approve; expected findings and the ObservedWriteScope ban; three reviewer moments; F43 hard-rule needles). scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts checkApprovalLexicon iterates LEXICON_SKILLS and fails if any of the four copies' approval_lexicon block lacks an F152 needle. scripts/check-teaching-surface.test.ts covers a copy that has the lexicon and named non-approvals but lacks an F152 needle. Failure conditions: assertions sample one skill; packaged copies are assumed rather than iterated or mirror-checked; existing C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT pins drop.
